question: Which L2 regularization strength minimizes 5-fold CV Brier score in logistic regression?
rationale: Testing across the prescribed range [0.0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0] using 5-fold contiguous CV with exact optimization procedure (GD 200 iter, lr=0.1, clipping [-30,30]) to identify empirically optimal regularization without search bias
decision: Fit logistic models with all 5 lambda values, use contiguous 5-fold splits, measure Brier score for each fold, average within lambda, select argmin
expected_effect: Will identify the lambda that provides best generalization; expect some improvement over baseline (lambda=0) if regularization helps, or lambda=0 if unregularized is optimal
falsifier: If the lowest Brier is not uniquely identified among the 5 lambda values tested, or if Brier computation deviates from (predicted_probs - labels)^2 mean

question: Do interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) significantly reduce Brier score in paired comparison?
alternatives: Fit both raw and interaction features, compare via paired t-test with threshold t=2.0
rationale: Paired t-test on fold-wise Brier scores (raw - interaction) is standard for evaluating feature engineering impact; t > 2.0 provides ~95% confidence threshold for unidirectional improvement in small samples
decision: Fit two models (raw features, raw+interaction features) with lambda=0.1, extract Brier per fold, compute paired t-stat across 5 folds, set interaction_helps=true iff t > 2.0
expected_effect: Either interactions significantly reduce error (t > 2.0) or do not (t <= 2.0); this accurately reflects whether feature engineering adds real signal
falsifier: If t-test is incorrectly computed (wrong DOF, wrong pairing, wrong direction) or if Brier per fold does not use consistent hold-out test set

question: Which model compression (sparsity %, bit quantization) retains the most dense-model Brier performance?
rationale: Fit dense model on all rows with lambda=0.1, apply sparsity by zeroing smallest-magnitude weights (k=round(p*d)), quantize remaining to 2^bits levels uniformly, measure retention = dense_brier / compressed_brier; select max retention
decision: Fit dense model once on full dataset (lambda=0.1), apply each of 6 compression configs on in-sample predictions, compute retention for each, report config with highest retention
expected_effect: Compression will degrade performance; configurations balancing sparsity and bit width should retain ~0.8-1.0 of dense performance, with higher retention indicating better trade-off
falsifier: If retention < 0.5 for all configs (indicating catastrophic degradation), or if sparsity/quantization is applied incorrectly (e.g., biased selection of weights, non-uniform quantization)
